question: If tan² θ = 1 - a², then the value of sec θ + tan³ θ cosec θ is:
solution:
**Given:**

tan2 θ = 1 - a2

**Concept Used:**

Secθ = 1/cosθ, tanθ = sinθ/cosθ, sinθ = 1/cosecθ

Sec2θ – tan2θ = 1

**Calculation:**

Secθ = 1/cosθ, tanθ = sinθ/cosθ, sinθ = 1/cosecθ

Sec2θ – tan2θ = 1

We have to calculate, sec θ + tan3 θ cosec θ

begin{array}{l} = (1)/({cos theta )} + frac{{si{n³}theta }}{{co{s³}theta }} times (1)/({sintheta )}\ = (1)/({cos theta )}[ {1 + frac{{si{n²}theta }}{{co{s²}theta }}} ]\ = (1)/({cos theta )} times (1)/({co{s²)theta }} = (1)/({co{s³)theta }} end{array}

Now, given that,

tan2θ = 1 – a²

⇒ sec2θ – 1 = 1 – a2

begin{array}{l} Rightarrow (1)/({co{s²)theta }} = 2 - {a²}\ Rightarrow (1)/({co{s³)theta }} = {[ {2 - {a²}} ]⁽³⁾/⁽²⁾} end{array}
